notes: Prompt targets live under .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md (a skill is a directory, not a single file). A skill's invocable /name comes from the directory name, never the SKILL.md filename and never a name: frontmatter field (that only sets a display label for personal/project skills).

Targets marked targetRenamed:true deliberately do not use the default source-derived directory name. Copilot's 'name:' frontmatter values were used as the directory names to preserve /crp, /e, and /read-project-instructions.

Corrected 2026-08-26: disable-model-invocation:true does NOT remove a skill/command from the registry - it only stops Claude auto-invoking it; /name still works. A previous version of this note claimed otherwise; that was wrong. The skill now sets disable-model-invocation:true on crp specifically, because it commits/pushes and must only ever run when explicitly typed as /crp, per CLAUDE.md's 'NEVER auto-commit/push' rule.
The .claude/commands/ directory has been retired in favour of .claude/skills/ (migrated 2026-08-26). Do not recreate .claude/commands/*.md for these sources.
Do not re-create the pre-rename directory names on a future sync run; that would register duplicate skills.

2026-08-30: reconciled the phantom drift from commit 2f18a2cb (2026-08-27, 'add name field to skill frontmatter'), which hand-edited every skill's frontmatter after its last sync. Those targets' BODIES are byte-identical to their sources, so their recorded hashes were refreshed to current state - no target content was written. Note the name: field is cosmetic here: a skill's invocable /name comes from its directory.

2026-08-30: CLAUDE.md target drift is structural, not a problem - it is a merge target carrying a hand-written '## Claude-specific' section this skill never writes into. Its hash is refreshed to mean 'last state reconciled'. Verified this run: all 21 source headings are present in CLAUDE.md, nothing to merge.

2026-08-30: five entries now carry divergentByDesign:true with a divergenceReason. Their targets will always differ from their sources, because each difference is a platform feature with no counterpart on the other side - not drift, and not work outstanding. Report them as expected rather than actionable, and NEVER sync over them in either direction. The flag records intent, not state: the recorded hashes still move when either side genuinely changes, so a real edit is still detectable. Anything these entries do NOT name as platform-specific is ordinary drift and should be reconciled as usual.

files.divergenceReason: One cross-reference only: the source points at `.github/instructions/components.instructions.md`, the target at `.claude/rules/components.md`. That rewrite is this skill's own permitted edit - a Copilot path pointed at its Claude equivalent - so the sync reproduces it every run. Expected output, not drift.

Argument passing: the Claude copy uses `$ARGUMENTS`, which has no Copilot equivalent, and says '(Claude)' where the Copilot copy says 'you'. The Claude copy also carries skill frontmatter with no Copilot counterpart (argument-hint, allowed-tools, disable-model-invocation). Markdown table whitespace also differs because Prettier formats the Claude side. The substantive instructions are identical - do not sync either way.
The Claude copy names `ide_selection` tags, which is how a selection reaches Claude Code and has no Copilot equivalent. Everything else is identical.

Copilot has a `get_errors` tool; Claude does not, so the Claude copy falls back to the project's own linters. Syncing either direction would replace a working tool call with a workaround, or vice versa.
How the plan document arrives: Copilot attaches it to the prompt, Claude takes a path via `$ARGUMENTS`. Both say to ask rather than guess when it is absent.

Reads different files by design: copilot-instructions.md and instructions/ on the Copilot side, CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/ on the Claude side. The Claude copy also notes that those load automatically at session start.
